scope: Follow-up 14 regular-lab requested scenario; not complete original §19 acceptance or physical arm64 proof
title: Offline catch-up and new-node inheritance
expected: Accepted 1.0.1 remains current before the later 1.0.2 result; offline batch targets complete consistently with real results; a new node inherits fleet default through its own job without changing the old snapshot
actual: Offline target caught up through a real success result; a later new node inherited 1.0.2 through its own successful first-sync job; original snapshot unchanged

values, but cannot change current/last-good or clear recovery.","source":"docs/updates/central-lifecycle.md:545"},{"quote":"Once a result is accepted, seeding closes even for later jobs in that incarnation.","source":"docs/updates/central-lifecycle.md:626"},{"quote":"A mismatch in
either release keeps `unconfirmed=true` by withholding that job's observation
timestamp; a later agreeing report can confirm it.","source":"docs/updates/central-lifecycle.md:546"},{"quote":"A generation-bearing heartbeat is attributed to the **node's current job only**
(§13.2, §13.8; D-068, r13 M-1).","source":"docs/updates/central-lifecycle.md:554"},{"quote":"Before that incarnation's first accepted result, pre-result heartbeat seeding
fills **only a null `nodes.current_release_id`**","source":"docs/updates/central-lifecycle.md:574"},{"quote":"On the current job, each distinct unexpected release/job pair
gets one `update_observation.unexpected_release` audit","source":"docs/updates/central-lifecycle.md:599"},{"quote":"A
later agreeing null last-good permits the issued target to fill the null
`current_release_id`, without establishing `last_good_release_id`.","source":"docs/updates/central-lifecycle.md:621"}]
